s: Today is review day, so we look back at words from the last three days.
We just make the words you already know stronger.
Beans are small seeds we eat as food.
I eat beans for breakfast, and beans with rice for lunch.
Yes, I agree with you about beans.
Carrots are orange, and I eat carrots in soup.
Chips are thin pieces of fried potato.
I like fish and chips for lunch, but not every day.
Chips are fun food, but beans and carrots are better every day.
I think you agree with me on that one.
Actually, let me tell you a small story.
Actually, I thought chips were healthy, but actually they are not.
Actually, beans and carrots are the healthy choice.
That word, actually, means what is true or real.
I thought it was easy, but actually it was hard.
That is how we use actually.
When you shop online, you add to basket.
You click, and you add to basket.
You add to basket one thing, then you add to basket one more thing.
Then you check your basket and you pay.
And in town, where do you leave your car?
I left my car in the car park.
The car park is near the shops.
I walk from the car park to the shops, and I carry my shopping home.

Many people live in Africa, and they speak many languages.
Do you want to visit Africa?
I think Africa is a great place to learn about.
Asthma makes it hard to breathe.
My friend has asthma and uses an inhaler.
When asthma comes, she rests and uses her inhaler, and then she can breathe well again.
Asthma does not stop her from playing.
Your brain helps you think and learn new things.
Your brain is inside your head.
When you learn a word, your brain keeps it.
A strong brain loves beans, carrots, and sleep.
Let us not forget the other words from the last three days.
Blood is the red liquid inside your body.
Your body needs food and water.
Beer is a drink made from grain, but it is for adults only.
An aspirin is a small medicine for pain.
And your address is the number and street where you live.
Now you know all of them again.
I say a word, you say what it means.
